answer: Require each agent to hold a unique, randomly assigned data shard and answer surprise retrieval challenges. Like a marble that cannot be in two hands at once, one shard cannot serve two identities at once: when the network sends a sudden pulse of concurrent audits, Sybils sharing storage or bandwidth miss deadlines and lose deposits. A zephyr of cheap fake accounts gains no speed, because each new identity must provision its own shard, bandwidth, and deposit before acting, so mass forgery scales in real cost, not just in names.
